@graph.name: Synthetic Example Records
@graph.description: A synthetic Cascade Bridge Adapter package, and the only package this repository holds. It exists so that the lint published from here is exercised by the thing it is published for, against a subject this repository owns: no real adapter is cloned, named or pinned, which is the rule fixtures/README.md and pinning.md state. Everything in it is invented. The format, its schemas, its records, its releases and its vocabulary are made up; every URL that is not this repository's own is under example.org, IANA's reserved example domain, and none of them resolves. Its queries are real SPARQL 1.1: a mapping and a findings query that produce the expected graph and findings from its input, and a detect query. Committed files carry a sha256 computed over the committed bytes; two of them additionally carry an md5 standing for the digest a publisher publishes beside the file at its source, so that check 4 of adapter/validation.md has both kinds of claim to recompute and can be seen telling them apart.

@graph.name: set
@graph.description: The envelope an invented service returns: many records under a set root the format's own schema does not declare, so this envelope names the wrapper schema this package adds. The arrangement that makes check 5 of adapter/validation.md prefer an envelope's bridge:documentSchema to the adapter's bridge:sourceSchema.

@graph.name: record
@graph.description: One bare record, the document root the format's own schema declares. It names no bridge:documentSchema, so an input arriving in it is validated against the adapter's bridge:sourceSchema: the fallback branch of check 5.

@graph.name: Cascade Bridge Adapter profile
@graph.description: The RO-Crate 1.2 Profile Crate a conforming adapter package names in conformsTo. The IRI does not dereference; the Profile Crate describing it is adapter/profile/ro-crate-metadata.json in this repository, and bridge:specPin says at which commit.

@graph.name: sparql-1.1
@graph.description: The Bridge profile the adapter's SPARQL 1.1 queries run under, which every adapter requires.

@graph.name: cascade-bridge-spec at 0af0fc9
@graph.description: The one entity here that names something real: a tagged revision of the Cascade Bridge Specification, v0.2.0. A package inside the repository it pins cannot pin a release that contains it, so this pin trails the shapes the package conforms to (fixtures/README.md). A real adapter's workflow calls the lint at the matching ref and the lint fails a disagreement; this package is validated from inside the repository the pin names, by local path, so there is no ref to resolve and the pin is reported and not compared. A web-based data entity, referenced and not committed: the RO-Crate 1.2 validator reads every SoftwareSourceCode as a script that must be a File in hasPart.

@graph.name: synthetic vocabulary at the null commit
@graph.description: The vocabulary pin of an adapter whose vocabulary is invented. The SHA is git's null object id, forty zeros, so that nobody reads this as a commit that could be checked out; the repository is under example.org and does not resolve. A real adapter pins the Cascade vocabularies it writes, at a tagged commit of the spec repository, and the lint never dereferences either.

@graph.name: Synthetic example vocabulary
@graph.description: The invented namespace the expected graph is written in. Deliberately not cascade: or genomics:: a fixture in this repository must not read as an assertion about a Cascade vocabulary, and no Cascade term is minted here.

@graph.name: Mapping
@graph.description: The adapter's bridge:mapping: a SPARQL 1.1 CONSTRUCT turning one ExampleRecord unit into one ex:Record.

@graph.name: Findings query
@graph.description: The adapter's bridge:findingsQuery: a SPARQL 1.1 SELECT whose rows, one per Note, are the unit's findings.

@graph.name: Detect query
@graph.description: The adapter's bridge:detectQuery: a SPARQL 1.1 ASK, true for a bare record or a set holding at least one.

@graph.name: Example record XSD, pinned copy
@graph.description: The adapter's bridge:sourceSchema: the schema that declares the unit, ExampleRecord. It stands in for a schema pinned byte for byte from a publisher, so it carries two digests that say different things. sha256 is the local claim, computed over the committed bytes. md5 stands for the digest the publisher publishes beside the file at its source; here the source is invented, so it is the md5 of these same bytes, which is what a copy that has not drifted looks like. Check 4 recomputes both and reports a mismatch in each differently.

@graph.name: Example set XSD, this package's wrapper
@graph.description: The document schema of the set envelope: it includes the source schema and adds the set root the publisher's schema does not declare. Written by this package rather than copied, so it carries a local sha256 and no publisher's digest.

@graph.name: Test manifest
@graph.description: The cases a Bridge's harness would execute, and how each is judged. This package's own file, edited whenever a case is added, so no digest is recorded for it: a digest on a file that is meant to change is a digest that goes stale in the commit that changes it.

@graph.name: Synthetic input, set envelope
@graph.description: Two invented records, EX000001 and EX000002, in the set envelope. Written here rather than fetched from anywhere, so the crate records only the local claim about it.

@graph.name: Synthetic input, record envelope
@graph.description: One invented record, EX000003, in the record envelope, standing in for a document copied byte for byte from a publisher. sha256 is the local claim over the committed bytes; md5 stands for the publisher's, and matches because this copy has not drifted from a source that does not exist. The envelope declares no document schema, so check 5 validates this file against the adapter's bridge:sourceSchema.

@graph.name: Expected graph for example-0001
@graph.description: The graph the package's mapping produces from example-0001.xml, one ExampleRecord unit at a time. Written by hand. Check 6 parses it and stops there: comparing it with what the mapping produces is a Bridge's job.

@graph.name: Expected findings for example-0001
@graph.description: The findings the package's findings query produces beside that graph: one entry, for the free-text note the invented vocabulary has no term for, its sourceField a path from the unit. The four-field shape adapter/fixtures/README.md records as what an adapter writes today, with the standard form still open.

@graph.name: Synthetic example release, 2026-01
@graph.description: A referenced release that does not exist, under IANA's reserved example domain, so that this package holds one entity whose bytes are not committed. The lint never fetches it: check 4 records its digest without comparing it, and check 5 reports that the test naming it validates nothing here. Size and md5 are placeholders and are marked as such by being round numbers no real file would have.
